name: CA-19
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent party
Panetta holds a roughly 40-to-1 fundraising edge ($5.5M cash vs. $7K for Verbica)
No outside spending against Panetta and no competitive-race ratings
Prediction markets price Panetta at about 98 percent
model.rationale: The D+18 district, Panetta's overwhelming cash advantage, and the complete absence of outside spending against him all point to an easy incumbent win, and prediction markets agree at 98 percent. With no polls or ratings suggesting anything otherwise, the fundamentals justify keeping the seat firmly in the Safe D column.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Verbica or polling surprises in a low-information race could widen uncertainty, though not plausibly enough to put the outcome in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 19th District leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Jimmy Panetta is seeking another term against Republican Peter Coe Verbica. The district's roughly 18-point Democratic partisan lean gives any Republican nominee a steep climb, and no expert ratings flag the seat as competitive. Prediction markets put Panetta's chances around 98 percent.

The financial picture underscores the imbalance: Panetta has raised about $3.5 million and holds $5.5 million on hand, while Verbica has raised under $90,000 with roughly $7,000 remaining. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and no public general-election polls are available, so fundamentals carry the forecast. The expectation is a wide, comfortable win for Panetta in a district his party has held easily.
